tasks.design: Configure native transport/storage guideline links and retained equipment/product context in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the plant operations viewer and operator log. The operator monitors actual conditions and captures/checks the real required observations before saving; no automated safety clearance or control action is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated guideline navigation and log context entry can surround actual monitoring.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plant-record links and log context can reuse existing identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Actual hazardous conditions and compliance with the site method require direct operational judgment.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated context handling in actual logged monitoring.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-4 with operations and the log administrator, including staff consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native plant guideline links and operator-log context can reduce record handling while hazardous-product monitoring remains operator work.

assumptions: This is an actual monitoring episode with an existing required operator log. No additional safety report or certificate is invented.

Operations supplies actual site guidelines/status; the operator produces observations in s2 and captures/checks them in s3. No new structured sensor feed, compliance flag or inferred safe state is assumed.
Native configuration first; existing equivalent links/context remove the gain. Missing or stale status requires actual operator investigation, not a model conclusion.

unknowns: Actual log requirements and existing native context

tasks.short: Read logsheets for demand, disposition and malfunctions

steps.what: Select and check the actual shift logsheets, demand/disposition records, time window, equipment tags and existing historian values
inputs: actual operator-produced digital logsheets and historian values
actual demand/disposition question and relevant shift/equipment identities
outputs: operator-checked actual log source set, time/tag mapping and gaps

steps.what: Apply actual approved limit and trend rules to the checked log values and assemble demand/disposition totals, flagged changes and source links without deciding the fault
inputs: operator-checked actual log source set, time/tag mapping and gaps
actual operations-approved demand, limit and trend definitions
outputs: rule-derived demand/disposition view and limit/trend exceptions with source links

steps.what: Review a bounded source-linked extraction of relevant free-text log events, checking every retained event and uncertain wording against the actual log entry
inputs: operator-checked actual log source set, time/tag mapping and gaps
rule-derived demand/disposition view and limit/trend exceptions with source links
outputs: operator-checked relevant log events and unresolved wording with exact source references

loop.purpose: Find relevant meaning in actual free-text log entries alongside fixed rules
loop.input: Actual selected log entries and the operator's demand/disposition/malfunction question
loop.output: Proposed relevant events with exact log-entry references and uncertainty
loop.check: Operator opens every retained source and checks meaning, timing and contradictions; no model-only exclusion of unreviewed events
loop.stop: Missing source, conflicting wording or unsupported event returns to direct manual log reading
loop.why_not_simpler: Tag/limit rules cannot determine the meaning of free-text operator observations

steps.what: Read and interpret the actual logsheets and checked views to determine product demand and disposition or detect possible malfunctions, retaining uncertainty and deciding any required investigation
inputs: rule-derived demand/disposition view and limit/trend exceptions with source links
operator-checked relevant log events and unresolved wording with exact source references
actual original logsheets and current operating context
outputs: operator's actual demand/disposition interpretation and suspected malfunctions requiring investigation

tasks.design: Configure native limit/trend and demand views in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the actual historian and digital operator log, before adding bounded source-linked reading of free-text entries. The operator checks actual sources and decides the operational meaning; all outputs remain reading aids with no control action or hidden notification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operators may repeat manual comparison of log values and free-text events across a shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Native historian rules handle explicit numeric checks; a bounded semantic step can propose relevant free-text events for direct source checking.
tasks.still_hard: Missing readings, ambiguous log wording and actual fault diagnosis require the operator.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a normal-looking trend conflicts with the actual plant state.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated log comparison while retaining operator interpretation.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-6 with operations, historian/log owners and staff consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native historian rules can flag explicit limits/trends and bounded source-linked reading can assist free-text log review; actual plant interpretation remains human work.

assumptions: The scenario has actual digital logs and existing historian values, produced by instruments and operators during their already-required rounds. Source selection, tag/time checks and gaps are counted in s1; no free transcription from paper is assumed. Paper or unsupported logs remain manual.

Operations supplies actual approved limits, units, intervals and total definitions. Missing/stale values, unmapped tags or undefined limits are flagged as gaps, not inferred safe states or invented demand.
Native rules/views first. Existing equivalent calculations and historian runtime earn no additional saving; s2 represents manual cross-log comparisons that the configured view actually replaces.

The semantic step only proposes events from supplied originals. All retained statements are source-checked and no unreviewed model exclusion is accepted. It does not diagnose faults or authorize operating changes.

Shares 25/25/20/30 are provisional unmeasured active effort. Gross saving 5 + 25 + 8 = 38; 4 hours of rule/source/model-output upkeep leaves 34 net. Actual source checking and final interpretation remain.
The task is reading/determination. No new handover report, save, send or control commit is silently added; actual follow-up contact is separately decomposed in task 14297.
unknowns: Actual digital log quality, existing native rules and manual comparison workload
research_questions: Observe missed/false flags and source-check effort before estimating any real saving.

already_counted.description: Actual source selection/checks, semantic source verification and operational interpretation remain.

incremental.description: Maintain tag/limit definitions and review source coverage and semantic extraction failures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 unmeasured range below provisional 34 percent net; conditional on actual manual cross-log comparisons and valid digital sources.

actual maintenance crew response

tasks.design: Configure native equipment-to-duty-contact navigation in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the plant maintenance contact directory. The operator still determines the real need, checks the final request and recipient and contacts the actual crew through {TELEPHONY}; no automatic notification or maintenance authorization is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current responsible crew can require repeated contact-directory navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment/duty directory links can expose existing maintained contacts.
tasks.still_hard: Problem facts, urgency and actual crew availability require operator and crew judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Communicate the real plant condition and recognize an inadequate or misunderstood response.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 with maintenance planning and directory access owners

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native maintained duty/contact links can reduce recipient lookup while actual maintenance communication remains human work.

assumptions: Maintenance planning supplies actual current duty contacts; the operator checks them in s2 and produces the actual problem/urgency in s1. No new availability feed or structured diagnosis is assumed.
Missing/stale contacts require manual routing. Native links first; equivalent existing directory settings remove the gain.

This is an actual internal voice-contact episode. It contains no required written ticket hidden in conversation and no invented follow-up report; if a real ticket is also required, its actual preparation and separate commit must be counted.
Shares 35/15/20/30 are unmeasured active effort. Gross saving 4.5 minus 1 hour of link upkeep leaves 3.5 net. Real phone communication remains fully retained, not treated as a negligible save.
The exact request and recipient are checked in ordinary preparation in s3 before s4. Changed facts or recipient require renewed checking; the conversation does not grant equipment-work permission.
unknowns: Actual duty-directory integration and internal versus contracted maintenance routing
research_questions: Measure time spent finding the current crew separately from problem assessment and actual contact.

tasks.still_hard: Timing, worker location and changing equipment state remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a misunderstood direction and adapt to the actual plant state.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live equipment-worker directions require actual condition checks and timely human communication; ordinary radios and displays already support the work.

assumptions: Actual state/worker observation is separated in s1, direction selection in s2 and communication in s3. No new structured command trigger or sensor feed is assumed.

The task is actual live direction, with no required report, log entry or permit write hidden in conversation. If the actual site requires such a record, decompose its observed capture/commit rather than inventing a baseline here.
Native display and radio settings are considered, but already-used functionality does not remove real observation, decision or communication. No software controls auxiliary equipment.
